text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real-world data on how it behaves across the entire codebase, not just edge cases. The trade-off is temporary overhead for reviewers, but it prevents missing systemic issues. After that, we’ll have the evidence to decide whether to expand or adjust.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode normalizes noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments, including the useful ones, because they can’t trust the tool’s output. A better alternative is to run PR-Agent on a *representative sample* of PRs first, then expand only if the signal-to-noise ratio proves acceptable. Settle it by measuring reviewer engagement metrics (e.g., comment resolution rate) after the sample run—if it’s below 30%, reject the tool.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* PRs from new contributors for two weeks first. This tests the tool’s value where it matters most—catching mistakes from less experienced developers—without wasting time on low-risk changes. After validating the signal-to-noise ratio, expand to all PRs if the tool proves useful.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us a full baseline of how it behaves across the entire codebase, not just edge cases. The trade-off is temporary reviewer fatigue from extra comments, but it prevents missing systemic issues that only appear in mainstream workflows. After that, we’ll have real data to decide whether to scale back or expand.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* new-contributor PRs for two weeks first.

Result: We get real-world data on signal-to-noise ratio where mistakes matter most, without wasting reviewer time on low-risk changes. Owned by Overhaul.
